info.title: ISN REST API
info.summary: Inspection Support Network — legacy REST API.
info.description:
The legacy REST API for the Inspection Support Network.

## Base URL

Every request is scoped to a **company key** — the tenant slug that identifies your
ISN account:

    https://inspectionsupport.com/{companyKey}/rest

White-label customers are served from their own domain (for example
`goisn.net`), so treat both the host and the company key as configurable.

## Authentication

HTTP Basic. Use your **access key** as the username and your **secret access
key** as the password. Generate them in ISN under *Settings -> My Access Keys*
(`/{companyKey}/access-keys`).

Two things to know: access keys **do not expire**, and they carry the **full
privileges of the user who owns them** — there is no per-key scoping. Treat them
as you would that user's password, and issue them from an account whose
privileges match what the integration actually needs.

Credentials may also be passed as `username` and `password` query parameters.
That path still works but is **deprecated**, logs a warning server-side, and
leaks credentials into access logs and browser history. Do not use it.

## Sending data

Content type is **not uniform across verbs**, and getting it wrong fails quietly
rather than with an error:

| Verb | Accepts |
|---|---|
| `GET` | query string |
| `POST` | `application/json` **or** `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`; fields may also be passed as query parameters |
| `PUT`, `DELETE` | `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` **only** |

`POST` reads a JSON body only when `Content-Type` begins with `application/json`;
otherwise it reads form fields. `PUT` and `DELETE` accept form encoding only — send
them JSON and every field arrives empty, with a `200` rather than an error. The
report and attachment upload endpoints are the exception: they take the raw file as
the body.

## Responses

There is no single response envelope. Most endpoints return a JSON object with a
`status` field (`ok` or `error`) and a payload key named after the resource, but
this is a convention rather than a guarantee and several endpoints deviate.
Each operation documents its own shape.

## Errors

An unrecognised endpoint returns **405**, not 404 — worth knowing if you are
checking for a path's existence. A `400` lists the required fields you left out.
A `403` means your credentials were accepted but the account behind them lacks the
privilege the endpoint needs.

## Rate limiting

This API is **not** rate limited. Please be a considerate client regardless —
poll on a sensible interval, use the `after` filter to fetch only what has changed,
and back off when you see an error.

## Path precedence

Some paths overlap — `/order/complete` and `/order/{id}` are both two segments.
Named segments always win over the parameter form, so `/order/complete` is the
complete-order action and never an order whose id happens to be `complete`.

## Scope of this document

This describes the customer-facing surface only. ISN-internal, partner-specific
and deprecated endpoints are deliberately excluded.

servers.description: ISN, scoped to your company key

host.description: Your ISN domain. White-label accounts use their own.

post.description:
Requires the **OWNER** privilege. One URL listening to one or more events.

Pass `order` to scope the webhook to one order: it then receives only events about that order.
Without it, the webhook receives the events for every order in the office. The order is fixed when
the webhook is created; to follow a different order, create another webhook.

The webhook is created in the office named by the `office` query parameter (the primary office
without it), and `order` must belong to that office. For an order in another office, send
`POST /webhooks?office=<office uuid>`.

`track` and `signed` default to **on**: a tracked webhook gets delivery history, retries and a
status; a signed one gets an `X-ISN-Signature` header on every delivery. Pass `false` to opt out.

The signing secret is returned **once**, as `secret`, in this response. No read returns it again;
store it now, or roll a new one with `POST /webhooks/{id}/secret`.

requestBody.description: Send either `application/json` or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. Form-encoded, `events` is a comma-separated string.

url.description: Where ISN delivers. Must be `https://`; payloads carry client names, addresses, emails and phone numbers.

order.description: Optional. The order's UUID (`order_id` in event payloads) or numeric id (`order_oid`). The webhook then receives only events about this order. Must be an order in the office the request is for. Pass that office's UUID as the `office` query parameter, or leave it out for the primary office. Any other order answers 404.

name.description: A label for the webhook, shown on the Webhooks page.

method.description: POST sends the payload as a JSON body; GET sends it as a querystring.

track.description: Keep delivery history and retry failed deliveries for about a day.

signed.description: Generate a signing secret and sign every delivery with it.

url.description: Where ISN delivers. Must be `https://`; payloads carry client names, addresses, emails and phone numbers.

order.description: Optional. The order's UUID (`order_id` in event payloads) or numeric id (`order_oid`). The webhook then receives only events about this order. Must be an order in the office the request is for. Pass that office's UUID as the `office` query parameter, or leave it out for the primary office. Any other order answers 404.

name.description: A label for the webhook, shown on the Webhooks page.

method.description: POST sends the payload as a JSON body; GET sends it as a querystring.

track.description: Keep delivery history and retry failed deliveries for about a day.

signed.description: Generate a signing secret and sign every delivery with it.

secret.description: The signing secret. Present only when `signed` is on, and only in this response.

delete.description: Requires the **OWNER** privilege. Stops all deliveries. A deleted webhook keeps its delivery history, and can be restored (paused) from the Webhooks page's *Show deleted* view. A Zap's webhook is normally removed by turning the Zap off; deleting one here needs a company owner (403 otherwise).

basicAuth.description: Access key as username, secret access key as password.

WebhookNotFound.description: No webhook with that `id` in this office, or it has been deleted. An unknown action (`/webhooks/{id}/<something else>`) also answers 404.

WebhookZapier.description: The user lacks the **OWNER** privilege, or the webhook belongs to a Zap (`zapier` is true). A Zap's events can never be changed here; pausing, resuming or deleting a Zap's webhook needs a company owner.

WebhookOrderNotFound.description: The `order` given is not an order in this office. Nothing was changed.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated, but the user lacks the required privilege.

WebhookBadRequest.description: Invalid input, with a `message` saying what to fix -- a URL that is not `https://`, a missing or unknown event (the message lists the valid names), or unsubscribing a webhook's last event. A malformed JSON body is also a 400. Nothing was changed.

WebhookOffice.name: office
WebhookOffice.description: Office UUID. Without it, the company's primary office. A webhook belongs to one office; another office's `id` answers 404. An `order` sent with the request must be an order in this office.

Webhook.description: One webhook. Never carries its signing secret.

id.description: The webhook's identifier, for the calls that take `{id}`. Usually a UUID; a webhook created through the JSON API's `/json/hooks` before it was grouped has `h` plus a number (`h1234`). Treat it as opaque.

tracked.description: Deliveries are recorded and failures retried.

zapier.description: Created by ISN's Zapier app. Its events and lifecycle belong to the Zap.

status.description: `failing` once a fifth or more of its recent deliveries failed.

delivered.description: Successful deliveries. null for an untracked webhook -- nothing is measured, which is not the same as zero.

failed.description: Failed deliveries. null for an untracked webhook.

error_rate.description: Percentage of recent deliveries that failed. null for an untracked webhook.

order_id.description: The UUID of the order this webhook is scoped to. null for a webhook that receives every order in the office.

order_oid.description: The same order's numeric id. null for an office-wide webhook.

WebhookEvents.description: Event names, as `GET /webhooks/events` lists them. The numeric event id is accepted too.
